rationale: Evidence from iteration 1 (score 160.6, up from 36.3): oval finished 2 of 20 trials and the other 18 went off track with max_error about 0.062 m, just above the 0.06 m off-track limit. s-bend and slalom ended off track in every trial, with max_error 0.062 to 0.064 m and one line-loss event per run. Steering oscillation was modest (0.19 to 0.32), so the derivative gain does not appear to be the problem. The failure is still speed-limited: at base_speed 1.2 with kp 5.0 and kd 0.8 the robot drifts past 0.06 m on the sharpest bends. Following the Evaluator's first branch (line loss present and max_error near 0.06 m), I lower base_speed from 1.2 to 1.0 and keep kp 5.0, kd 0.8, ki 0.02, sensor geometry and line_loss unchanged. This isolates the speed effect. Expected result: max_error below about 0.05 m on all tracks, fewer or no line-loss events, and a higher finish rate on the oval and s-bend. The trade-off is completion time: at 1.0 m/s average the 4 to 5 m course takes about 4.5 s or more, so the 3 s time term will be zero. Completion (500 points) and progress are the priority, and the time term can be recovered later once the robot holds the line. Hypotheses to check next: (a) the 1 to 2 line-loss events are caused by the sharpest bend rather than start-up; (b) max_error falls below 0.05 m at base_speed 1.0; (c) steering_oscillation stays near 0.3 with kd 0.8, so kd does not need changing yet. Measurements requested: completion, progress, completion time, rms and max error, line-loss events, steering oscillation, control effort, controller errors and noise robustness.
